List column names by tidyselect

Source: R/ds.R
names.Rd

List column names by tidyselect

Usage

ds(.data, ..., .type = c("vector", "table"))

Arguments

.data

A data frame, tibble, or data.table. ds() also accepts a character vector representing a name inventory, such as an earlier ds() result. Inventory entries must be unique, nonempty, and nonmissing; the vector's own names are ignored. An empty inventory is allowed.

...

<tidy-select> Existing columns to select or rename. Omit to include all columns. Computed columns are not created by this argument.

.type

"vector" (the default) returns the names as a character vector, like Stata's ds; "table" returns them as a one-column table.

Value

ds() returns a character vector. ds(.type = "table") returns a table with one character column, name. On ungrouped data, an empty selection returns a zero-length vector or a zero-row table, respectively. Tables preserve the input's data.frame, tibble, or data.table container and supported preview settings, but do not recreate grouping or arbitrary subclasses on the new rows.

Details

Selection order and renamed column names follow dplyr::select(). On a grouped data frame, selection retains grouping columns and can emit a message when they were not explicitly selected. Ungroup first to select independently of grouping columns. The input data are not modified. For character inventories, select by names, positions, or name helpers and rename as usual. Data-type predicates such as where(is.numeric) are not available because an inventory contains no column data.

See also

variables(), codebook(), browse()

Other inspection functions: browse(), codebook(), misstable(), var_type(), variables()

Examples

ds(lifeexp) # equivalent to names(lifeexp)
#> [1] "region"    "country"   "popgrowth" "lexp"      "gnppc"     "safewater"
ds(lifeexp, country:lexp)
#> [1] "country"   "popgrowth" "lexp"     
ds(lifeexp, where(is.character), .type = "table")
#> # A tibble: 1 × 1
#>   name   
#>   <chr>  
#> 1 country

starwars <- dplyr::starwars
ds(starwars, ends_with("color"), .type = "table")
#> # A tibble: 3 × 1
#>   name      
#>   <chr>     
#> 1 hair_color
#> 2 skin_color
#> 3 eye_color 

# Save a programmatic selection for later stages of a pipeline.
numeric_names <- ds(lifeexp, where(is.numeric))
dplyr::select(lifeexp, dplyr::all_of(numeric_names))
#> # A tibble: 68 × 5
#>    region               popgrowth  lexp gnppc safewater
#>    <dbl+lbl>                <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>
#>  1 1 [Europe & C. Asia]      -0.6    74   870        49
#>  2 1 [Europe & C. Asia]      -1.2    70   570        83
#>  3 1 [Europe & C. Asia]       0.1    78 27810        97
#>  4 1 [Europe & C. Asia]       0.9    64   510        49
#>  5 1 [Europe & C. Asia]      -0.5    68  1540        82
#>  6 1 [Europe & C. Asia]       0.2    77 26530       100
#>  7 1 [Europe & C. Asia]       1.8    74  1230        87
#>  8 1 [Europe & C. Asia]      -0.7    71  1440        90
#>  9 1 [Europe & C. Asia]      -0.1    72    NA        85
#> 10 1 [Europe & C. Asia]      -0.1    75  6140        95
#> # ℹ 58 more rows
ds(numeric_names, dplyr::starts_with("pop"))
#> [1] "popgrowth"
